clue.text: Detailed new firm to deliver painting

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, the word for new loses its last letter

parts.note: new means fresh
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A newly founded company is hired to produce a highly detailed artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like praise for the painting but means de-tailed: FRESH loses its tail H, leaving FRES.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a type of painting done on wet plaster on a wall or ceiling.

clue.text: Den supports fellow showing talent

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports another sits beneath it, so the fellow goes on top

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: Someone who props up their study shows a natural gift.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'supports' puts F above LAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural aptitude or knack, the same as a talent.

clue.text: Hoard standard carpeting material

parts.note: stock as an adjective means standard, as in a stock answer
pile is the raised surface fibre of a carpet

explanation.surface: Someone lays in a big supply of ordinary carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpile is an accumulated store of goods, a reserve put by.

clue.text: Ham served to air corps in public

indicators.note: in tells us the air corps letters are placed inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means done openly, in public

explanation.surface: A ham sandwich is handed out to air force personnel in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like food served to the troops; it is the verb for exaggerated acting.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform theatrically with exaggerated gestures, as a poor actor does.

clue.text: Its hands produce everything needed

parts.note: a factory's hands are its workers, who make all the goods; the phrase for a factory is also slang for everything required

explanation.definitionFit: The full set of everything wanted is a colloquial idiom, and a factory or plant is also called by this name, staffed by hands.

clue.text: Men VIP protected sadly show hubris

indicators.note: sadly suggests the words are in a sorry state, so their letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Bodyguards protecting a VIP were, unhappily, overconfident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges MEN VIP PROTECTED, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt providence is to take a needless risk, the arrogant confidence the Greeks called hubris.

clue.text: Carry out order to inflict ultimate penalty

definitions.meaning: to carry out an instruction is to perform it
the ultimate penalty is death, so this means put to death

explanation.surface: Someone is told to carry out an order imposing a death sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to perform an instruction and to kill a condemned person as a punishment.

clue.text: A tirade resulting in discharge

indicators.note: resulting in says the letters of a tirade turn into something new

explanation.surface: A furious rant ends in someone being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resulting in' rearranges A TIRADE; 'discharge' looks like dismissal from a job but means give off, as heat or light.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to send out energy such as heat or light, to emit it.

clue.text: He's next in line after coup by soldiers

parts.note: a coup is a notable achievement, a success
OR is short for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: An heir apparent takes over after the army stages a coup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coup' looks like a military takeover but means a triumph, a success. OR (other ranks) is the crossword term for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A successor is the person who follows another in a post or title, the one waiting to take over.

clue.text: A bulwark built on land

parts.note: a shore is a prop or support, a bulwark against collapse

explanation.surface: A defensive wall is constructed on dry ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bulwark' suggests a sea wall, but SHORE here is a timber prop, as in shoring up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the beach or dry ground rather than at sea is the adverbial sense of the word.

clue.text: Furious when poor Diane appears in raincoat

indicators.note: in says the reworked name is put inside the coat

parts.note: a mac, short for mackintosh, is a raincoat

indicators.note: poor suggests the name is in bad shape and so rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is enraged when shabby Diane turns up wearing a mackintosh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' makes ENADI and 'in' sets it in the coat; mac is the everyday British word for a raincoat. The adjective comes from the frenzied female followers of Bacchus.
explanation.definitionFit: The maenads were the frenzied female followers of Bacchus, so the adjective means wild or raving.

clue.text: Stagger seaman by adding seasoning

parts.note: to stagger someone is to rock them, shake them
an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is knocked off balance when salt is thrown at him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagger' reads as reeling but means to shock, ROCK; SALT is an experienced sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse crystals of mineral halite are used to flavour food, a kind of seasoning.

clue.text: Give latest info about how to modernise

definitions.meaning: to bring someone current with news on a matter
to bring something up to current standards

explanation.surface: A guide explains the latest thinking on bringing things up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to brief someone with the newest news and to renovate or bring current.

clue.text: American man hems in leading MP

indicators.note: hems means surrounds, so the word for a man closes around the following little word

parts.note: mister is a common American way to address a man

explanation.surface: A US citizen corners a prominent politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hems' (surrounds) splits the address word after its first letter. 'Leading MP' is fair because a British minister is a senior member of Parliament holding government office.
explanation.definitionFit: A government minister is a senior member of parliament heading a department.

clue.text: To defame hard worker is evil

parts.note: to malign someone is to speak ill of them, to defame them
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: Slandering an industrious person is wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Malignant means wicked or spiteful, harmful in intent.

clue.text: Said medals won by compères

indicators.note: Said signals the medal letters are spoken, not written

parts.note: MC is the Military Cross, a British medal, so medals are MCs

explanation.surface: Presenters are reported to have won military decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: MC (Military Cross) is a British gallantry medal; 'MCs' spoken aloud spells out as the answer, the American word for hosts.
explanation.definitionFit: A compère hosts a show, a master of ceremonies, which Americans spell out phonetically.

clue.text: Specialist dealers serve many boxing managers

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, taken as many
handlers are the trainers and managers who look after a boxer

explanation.surface: Particular merchants supply numerous fight managers.
explanation.walkthrough: C (100) for 'many' is a crossword convention. A chandler is a specialist supplier, such as a ship's chandler selling gear to boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandler is a dealer in a particular line, originally candles, now often ship supplies.

clue.text: I learn about a type of equation

definitions.note: an adjective describing an equation, not a noun

indicators.note: about means around, the letters going round into a new order

explanation.surface: A student studies a kind of mathematical formula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges I LEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight-line equation of the first degree is called this, after a line on a graph.

clue.text: Ron must produce a remedy

indicators.note: to produce is to make something new, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Ron has to come up with a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' rearranges RON MUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack cure or pet panacea, a medicine of dubious worth.

clue.text: New lawyer gets little thanks for unchecked statistics

parts.note: raw means fresh or new, inexperienced
DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer
ta is a short British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A rookie attorney receives scant gratitude for figures nobody verified.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you; DA is the US District Attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw data are figures collected but not yet processed or verified.

clue.text: Countryman fails to finish foul beer

indicators.note: fails to finish means the word for foul loses its last letter

parts.note: foul means vile
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A rustic leaves his disgusting pint half drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: VILE without its final E gives VIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A countryman is someone who lives in a rural village, a rustic.

clue.text: Star unavailable to open proceedings

parts.note: the star of a show plays the lead
off means not available, as a dish that is off the menu

explanation.surface: The headline performer is absent for the opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unavailable' gives OFF as in a menu item no longer served.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead off is to begin, to take the first turn in an event.

clue.text: Industrial action in German capital by workers' leader

parts.note: Oslo is the capital of Norway

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word workers'

explanation.surface: A labour dispute erupts in a German city, led by a union figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German capital' suggests Berlin, but the capital is OSLO after G for German. A go-slow is a protest in which workers deliberately work slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-slow is a form of protest in which staff deliberately reduce their pace of work.

clue.text: Finding late love is a non-starter

parts.note: late means deceased, dead
duck is a British term of endearment, like love or dear

explanation.surface: Discovering romance late in life proves hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' looks like lateness but means deceased. 'Duck' as a term of endearment is regional British usage, in the Midlands and North.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan with no chance of success is called by this idiom, a hopeless case.

clue.text: Animal-house erected by a large African village

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means built upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: Noah's ark housed the animals

explanation.surface: A big barn for livestock is put up near an African settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns ARK upwards to KRA, as a down answer reads bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A kraal is a traditional southern African village of huts, often enclosing a cattle pen.

clue.text: Flying doctor gets own Scottish damp-proof system

parts.note: air as in air travel describes flying
ain is the Scots word for own

explanation.surface: A doctor in an air ambulance acquires a Scottish waterproofing system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying doctor' suggests an outback medic, but the phrase splits in two. The 'Scottish' word for own is a dialect form, and the answer is a building term.
explanation.definitionFit: An air drain is a cavity left around a building's foundations to keep walls dry.

clue.text: Does as ordered in the Ukraine

definitions.note: a place found in that country, standing for a city there

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone follows instructions while in the Ukraine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges DOES AS. The definition is the place's location, a city in the Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port city in Ukraine.

clue.text: Model has a little time in place of worship

indicators.note: in places the two short pieces inside the building for worship

parts.note: a temple is a building for worship
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A model pays a short visit to a shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the article and the time letter just before the final letter of the building. 'Model' is a pattern, not a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern or model used as a guide for making copies.

clue.text: Some cafes' talented clientele get merry

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Gifted customers at coffee shops become cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'clientele get merry' does not mean the answer: only 'merry' does, and 'clientele get' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Festal means festive, belonging to a feast or celebration, hence jolly.
